about.title: San Marino Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Marino's tree-lined streets carry a lot of local and cut-through traffic, and public records show 64 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, with 91 people hurt. Corridors like Huntington Drive, Los Robles Avenue, San Marino Avenue, and California Boulevard see the bulk of that volume, and Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to bring the most reports. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the moments right after matter: photos, witness names, and a slow approach to any insurance adjuster asking for a recorded statement. We handle personal injury claims under California law. Our team can review your situation, explain your options, and help you avoid common mistakes that can hurt a claim before it even gets started.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity was involved. Waiting to talk to someone can quietly cost you options you didn't know you had.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Be Argued Down
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces your payout. We can push back on inflated fault percentages an insurer might try to assign you.

items.title: No Cap Means Full Value Matters
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases. Our team can help make sure that side of your claim isn't overlooked or undervalued.

items.question: I was in a crash on Huntington Drive. Should I give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's usually best to hold off. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions in a way that can be used to reduce your claim later, even if you're just trying to be helpful. Our team can talk to them on your behalf so nothing you say gets twisted.

items.question: What if the crash happened at a city-maintained intersection in San Marino?
items.answer: Claims against government entities, including cities, come with a much shorter deadline, sometimes as little as six months instead of the standard two years. This is worth flagging early with an attorney so you don't miss that window.

items.question: Do you charge me anything?
items.answer: No. We handle your case on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover money. There is no fee to you unless we secure a recovery.
